title: bro CLI panics on EPIPE when stdout closes mid-print
wanted_capability: bro mcp call (and any bro subcommand printing large output) should exit quietly when its stdout reader closes early (jq that fails to parse, head, a broken pipe in a script), instead of the Rust default panic "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)" with a backtrace note. Observed spamming operator scripts when a downstream jq exited immediately; one panic per invocation. Standard fix is handling EPIPE on the print path (or restoring SIGPIPE default for the CLI).
fallback_used: Scripts buffer bro output to a temp file before parsing.
evidence: observed 2026-08-16: 12 consecutive 'thread main panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1166' while piping bro mcp call output into a jq that exited early
cosmetic only: exit path, no state touched
resolution_note: bro restores the default SIGPIPE disposition at the top of main (crates/bro-cli/src/main.rs restore_default_sigpipe, unix only), so a closed stdout reader ends the process quietly with SIGPIPE (exit 141) instead of the Rust EPIPE panic. Verified: `bro mcp call bbox_stats '{}' | false` went from exit 101 with a panic message to exit 141 silent.
